sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: A perennial herb in the humid tropical forests of Central America and northern South America. It develops upright stems and broad oval leaves; plants commonly grow to about 1 m.

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: As in other aroids, tiny flowers are packed on a spadix partly enclosed by a spathe. After pollination, the inflorescence may bear orange to red berries.

sections.title: Toxicity
sections.text: The tissues contain needle-shaped calcium oxalate crystals (raphides) that irritate the mouth and eyes. Ingestion can cause pain and swelling; do not taste the plant or handle sap with bare hands.
